overview.description: Dodo Payments is a Bengaluru-based startup that helps small software and AI companies sell their products worldwide. It bundles together payment processing, subscription billing, and handling all the local tax paperwork, so a small team doesn't have to figure out international tax rules or set up their own way to charge customers.
overview.industry: Fintech (financial technology) — online payments & billing tools
overview.vision: To become the default way that the next generation of digital products make money.
problemsSolved: Lets small software/AI teams sell to customers in other countries without having to register as a legal seller and handle taxes in every one of those countries themselves
Combines payments, subscription billing, and selling license keys/downloads into one tool instead of several separate ones
Supports billing models where customers pay based on how much they use (like per AI request), not just flat monthly fees
Reportedly approves new sellers faster than bigger competitors, according to some user accounts — especially helpful for independent developers in India

stats.monthlyUsers: The company claims 50,000+ builders/founders use it — this is a number the company reports about itself, not confirmed by an outside source
stats.revenue: Reported at about ₹9.0 lakh (roughly $10,800) for the 2025 financial year, per business-news outlet Inc42 — not confirmed by a second source

businessModel.summary: Charges a fee on each payment it processes for its customers — the same basic idea as competitors Paddle and Lemon Squeezy. The exact fee percentage isn't published anywhere or confirmed independently.

items.detail: Dodo officially becomes the seller on record for each purchase and takes a cut of every payment it processes on a customer's behalf.

items.stream: Tax handling included in the fee
items.detail: That same fee also covers dealing with tax paperwork, billing logic, fraud checks, and paying out the money — extra work a business would otherwise have to do itself.

items.name: Rishabh Goel
items.background: Previously worked at the fintech companies Wise and Prodigy Finance before co-founding Dodo Payments.

items.name: Ayush Agarwal
items.background: Previously started Tournafest, a platform for gamers, before co-founding Dodo Payments.

items.event: Rishabh Goel and Ayush Agarwal start Dodo Payments in Bengaluru to help SaaS/AI companies handle payments and billing.

Raises $1.1 million in its first outside funding round (announced Feb 25), with investment firms Antler, Venture Catalysts, and 100Unicorns, plus individual investors including a former a16z partner and someone previously connected to Oyo/Lightspeed.

Expands beyond payments/billing into helping sellers set up online storefronts and manage license keys, and launches Sentra, an AI assistant that helps manage billing and payments from inside a developer's coding tools.

items.investor: Antler, Venture Catalysts, 100Unicorns (firms); individual investors Nitin Gupta, Maninder Gulati, Raymond Russell, Preethi Kasireddy, Nishant Verman

items.challenge: Stripe now offers the same core service
items.details: In 2026, Stripe — a much bigger, more established payments company — launched its own version of what Dodo offers (becoming the seller-of-record and handling tax paperwork for digital businesses), built partly using a company it had acquired. Stripe has far more customers, brand recognition, and resources than Dodo does.

items.challenge: The investors listed on its own website don't match what's publicly confirmed
items.details: Dodo Payments' About page says it's backed by well-known investment firms Andreessen Horowitz, Lightspeed, Canaan, plus Visa, Goldman Sachs, and AWS. But the company's own funding announcement and independent company-data sites (Tracxn, Inc42) only show a $1.1 million first funding round from smaller firms (Antler, Venture Catalysts, 100Unicorns). The well-known firm names only show up because a couple of individual investors used to work there — not because those firms actually invested. Worth asking about directly if it comes up.

items.text: The interview includes a system-design conversation (about how to keep things reliable and handle unusual edge cases) plus a 1-2 day take-home coding assignment done solo, followed by a review discussion. Experience with the Rust programming language is a plus. This is based on only a couple of Glassdoor reviews and hasn't been checked against another source.

The few available reviews describe a culture that's growth-focused and hands-off (little micromanaging), with people given real ownership of their work — fitting for a small (~65-70 person) young company. Only 2 Glassdoor reviews exist, so treat this as a weak signal, not a solid read on what it's really like to work there.
